answer: A shared kernel of verified work history makes fake identities expensive: every agent reputation accrues only through completed, attested jobs, and a new identity starts at zero with no transferable credit. An attacker spinning up umber-shaded sockpuppets faces a long horizon before any of them can earn trust, because each must independently build the same costly track record. Sybil resistance comes from making identity itself the scarce resource — reputation is earned slowly, cannot be bought or cloned, and collapses the moment one puppet is caught cheating.
